description: Realistic coding prompts (English and Vietnamese) with the local tools a correct solution calls. Used by tests/verify-tool-selector.mjs to measure the task-selected tool schemas of the 'auto' mode: how many of `tools` the selector offers directly (recall) and what the offered schemas cost (the four router tools plus the offered local tools, estimateTokens over their JSON). To teach the selector a new word: add a prompt that needs it here first, watch the test fail, then extend GROUPS in lib/tool-selector.mjs.
labelling: tools lists the local tools (names as in LocalTools.definitions()) that a competent agent calls to finish the request, written from the request and the tool descriptions, not from what any selector offers.

Reads are listed when the request does not name the file (search_files, list_directory, read_file...), the mutation is listed (edit_file, write_file, delete_path, rename_symbol...), and a verification step is listed only when the request asks for it (run, test, build, check, open in the browser).
A dedicated tool wins over run_command when one exists (git_*, test_run, build_run, dependency_lookup, responsive_check); run_command is listed when none does (npm install, tsc, git reset).

kind is question | edit | bug-report | refactor | test-ci | git | browser-ui (a bug-report describes a symptom or pastes an error and has no verb that asks for a change); lang is en | vi. Prompts are NFC text. Some prompts use words the first selector already knew (fix, create, rename, commit, screenshot...) on purpose: they are controls that must keep working.

Entries with "source": "independent" (ids h..) were written, tools included, by a separate author who saw only the list of tools and not the selector; they were kept because they exposed a gap. The others were written together with the selector change.
